(sec-module-robotics.urdfimport)=
# Module: robotics.urdfImport

The import of robots from URDF files, through the Robotics Toolbox for Python (RTB) of P. Corke and
J. Haviland: the internal models of the RTB, a URDF file, and the data of a robot for Robot and its graphics;
MakeCorkeRobot, an RTB robot of the DH parameters of a robot dictionary of exudyn.robotics.models

- **Date**: 2023-04-15

(sec-urdfimport-getroboticstoolboxinternalmodel)=
## Function: GetRoboticsToolboxInternalModel

[`GetRoboticsToolboxInternalModel(modelName = '', ignoreURDFerrors = True)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L32)

- **function description**: Interface to roboticstoolbox (RTB) for loading internal robot models: the model of roboticstoolbox.models.URDF of this name, read from its URDF or xacro file. See the github project of roboticstoolbox-python of P. Corke and J. Haviland for more details. The model name is the short name used internally in the RTB. For available names, see the list roboticstoolbox.models.URDF.__all__ !
- **input**:
  - `modelName`: string for model, such as UR5, Puma560, Panda or LBR
  - `ignoreURDFerrors`: not used; kept for the scripts that pass it
- **output**: returns dictionary with 'robot' (RTB Robot class), 'urdf' (None; the visuals are in the links of the robot), 'urdfBasePath' (the xacro directory of the rtb-data package) and 'urdfFilePath' (the file that was read)
- **notes**: requires the Robotics Toolbox for Python 1.5 (pip install roboticstoolbox-python); its models UR3, UR5, UR10, KinovaGen3, Jaco, Fetch and PR2 are read through the package robot_descriptions, which downloads them on first use; Puma560, Panda, LBR, AL5D and the Interbotix robots (px150, vx300, wx250, ...) are part of the RTB's data. Some models do not include mass and inertia and therefore will not run as dynamic models (#3280)


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/serialRobotURDF.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/serialRobotURDF.py) (Ex)


(sec-urdfimport-loadurdfrobot)=
## Function: LoadURDFrobot

[`LoadURDFrobot(urdfFilePath, urdfBasePath, gripperLinks = None, manufacturer = '')`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L68)

- **function description**: Interface to roboticstoolbox (RTB) of P. Corke and J. Haviland. Use this function for loading urdf/xacro files.
- **input**:
  - `urdfFilePath`: string relative to urdfBasePath, representing xacro or urdf file
  - `urdfBasePath`: string representing the base path of the urdf or xacro directory for the respective robot, the directory of its ROS package; meshes given as package://<name>/... are found there and in the directories next to it
  - `gripperLinks`: list of link numbers representing gripper (as used internally in RTB Robot class)
  - `manufacturer`: the manufacturer, stored in the RTB robot
- **output**: returns dictionary with 'robot' (RTB Robot class), 'urdf' (None; the visuals are in the links of the robot), 'urdfBasePath' and 'urdfFilePath'
- **notes**: requires the Robotics Toolbox for Python 1.5 (pip install roboticstoolbox-python), which reads the file by xacrodoc (#3280). Note that some models do not include mass and inertia and therefore will not run as dynamic models!


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/serialRobotURDF.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/serialRobotURDF.py) (Ex)


(sec-urdfimport-completeinertiasfrommeshes)=
## Function: CompleteInertiasFromMeshes

[`CompleteInertiasFromMeshes(robotData, density = 1000., verbose = 1)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L162)

- **function description**: An estimate for the links of GetURDFrobotData whose mass or inertia is missing or not physical (#3357). A mesh gives the surface, not the interior of a link with its hollow arms, drives and cables, so that only one overall density of the enclosed volume makes sense, around 1000 kg/m^3; the inertials of a URDF which are correct always remain. A link with a mass but without a positive definite inertia gets the inertia of the solid of its meshes, scaled to the mass; a link without mass gets the mass, center of mass and inertia of that solid with the density. The principal moments are then raised as little as possible to fulfill the triangle inequality.
- **input**:
  - `robotData`: the dict of GetURDFrobotData
  - `density`: the overall density of the volume enclosed by the meshes of a link, in kg/m^3, used for the links without mass
  - `verbose`: 0 .. no output, 1 .. the links which remain without a physical mass or inertia
- **output**: a new dict of the same form; 'inertiaProblems' of each link tells what was changed, with ' (corrected)' at each problem, or what remains
- **notes**: the result is an estimate; store it with the Robot (Robot.SaveToHDF5), where it can be read and corrected


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`urdfCompleteInertiasTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/urdfCompleteInertiasTest.py) (TM)


(sec-urdfimport-readcolladamesh)=
## Function: ReadColladaMesh

[`ReadColladaMesh(fileName)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L199)

- **function description**: The triangles of a Collada (.dae) file with the diffuse colors of their materials, which pymeshlab does not keep (#3398); the transformations of the nodes, the unit and the up axis are applied, and the polygons of a polylist are split into triangles.
- **input**:
  - `fileName`: the .dae file
- **output**: a dict with 'points', 'normals' and 'colors' (RGBA), one per row, and 'triangles', the indices of their points, or None if a material has a texture or the file has no triangles


(sec-urdfimport-geturdfrobotdata)=
## Function: GetURDFrobotData

[`GetURDFrobotData(robot, urdf = None, linkColorList = None, staticJointValues = None, returnStaticGraphicsList = False, exportMesh = False, verbose = 1, densityForInertiaEstimation = None, toolLinkName = None, collision = False)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L322)

- **function description**: Interface to roboticstoolbox (RTB) of P. Corke and J. Haviland and Pymeshlab to import robot model and visualization into a struture readable by Exudyn. NOTE that this function is to be seen as a starting point for import, while some models have to be imported differently, in particular for joints that are not revolute or prismatic (in this case, copy function into local file and modify)!
- **input**:
  - `robot`: a RTB Robot (class) model, as returned e.g. by LoadURDFrobot
  - `urdf`: not used: the visuals and their origins are those of the links of robot (#3280)
  - `linkColorList`: if not None, this can contain a list of RGBA color lists for each link to prescribe colors instead of using internally stored colors or general color information (.obj files, the materials of .dae files, see ReadColladaMesh); set linkColorList=[graphics.color.red]*8 to set 8 link colors red; links are counted as in the urdf file and may be different from the number of joints
  - `staticJointValues`: if not None, has to be a list of joint angles (or displacements) for computing the static graphics list
  - `returnStaticGraphicsList`: return a list of GraphicsData which can be put into a ground to check visualization for zero joints, using: mbs.CreateGround(graphicsDataList=staticGraphicsList)
  - `exportMesh`: if True, the returned dict also contains a meshSetList which refers to the MeshSet in pymeshlab, which can be used for debugging purposes
  - `verbose`: 0 .. no output printed (only exceptions), 1 .. warnings, 2 .. further information
  - `densityForInertiaEstimation`: None, or the overall density of the volume enclosed by the meshes in kg/m^3, around 1000: a joint link without any inertial data gets the mass, center of mass and inertia of that solid; a mesh that does not close gives an estimate only; for partly given data see CompleteInertiasFromMeshes (#3357). Every link reports the problems of its mass and inertia in 'inertiaProblems', and they are printed with verbose > 0 (#3282)
  - `toolLinkName`: if not None, the name of the link of the tool frame; the frame of this link relative to the last joint link is returned in 'toolHT', for RobotFromURDFdata (#3356)
  - `collision`: if True, each joint link gets 'collision' and the dict the key 'collisionBase' for the links fixed to the base: a list of the collision geometries of the URDF in the frame of the link, also those of the links fixed to it: {'type': 'box', 'size': ..., 'HT': ...}, {'type': 'cylinder', 'radius': ..., 'length': ..., 'HT': ...}, {'type': 'sphere', 'radius': ..., 'HT': ...} and {'type': 'mesh', 'points': ..., 'triangles': ...}; the box and the axis of the cylinder are centered in HT, a 4x4 matrix; RobotFromURDFdata puts them into the collision shapes of the robot; a mesh needs pymeshlab (#3382)
- **output**: returns dictionary with items linkList (the joint links, each with its name, jointName, jointNumber (the index of the joint in the toolbox, as in staticJointValues), preHT relative to the joint link above, its parentName, mass, com, inertiaCOM, jointType, jointLimits and graphicsDataList; a parent before its children, else in the order of the links of the toolbox), numberOfJoints, baseLinkNames (the names of the links fixed to the base), graphicsBaseList (the graphics of the links fixed to the base), graphicsToolList (empty: the links fixed after the last joint are in the graphics of that link), staticJointValues and staticGraphicsList; a link of the URDF without joint (a fixed joint) moves with the joint link above it, which gets its graphics and its mass (#3280); a flipped joint (axis -1 in the URDF) has the same joint coordinate in a link frame turned by pi, flipHT of the link (#3282); the visuals of the URDF are its meshes and its boxes, cylinders and spheres (#3393)
- **notes**: requires installation (pip install) of roboticstoolbox-python and pymeshlab; if pymeshlab is not installed, a warning is raised and the meshes are ignored


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/serialRobotURDF.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/serialRobotURDF.py) (Ex)


(sec-urdfimport-reduceurdfrobotdata)=
## Function: ReduceURDFrobotData

[`ReduceURDFrobotData(robotData, lockedJoints = None, removedLinks = None)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L669)

- **function description**: Leave out joints and links in the data of GetURDFrobotData, for example the fingers of a gripper (#3372); needs neither the Robotics Toolbox nor a file.
- **input**:
  - `robotData`: the dict of GetURDFrobotData; it is not changed
  - `lockedJoints`: None or a dict {name: value}, name the joint of the URDF or its link, value the joint value at which it is fixed; the link is merged into the joint link above it: mass, center of mass and inertia added by the parallel axis theorem, the graphics moved, its children attached to that link. A locked link at the root has its graphics in the base, and its mass is lost as the base has none
  - `removedLinks`: None or a list of names of links (or their joints) which are left out with all links below them, with their mass and graphics; only the first n links of a serial robot: the name of link n+1
- **output**: a new dict of the same form, with numberOfJoints, staticJointValues and inertiaProblems updated; the 'toolHT' relative to the last remaining link, for the tool frame at zero joint values (a tool on a locked link at a value other than zero is not moved with it); staticGraphicsList is empty, as it shows the robot before the reduction

*example*:

```python
  data = GetURDFrobotData(robot, toolLinkName='panda_hand')
  data = ReduceURDFrobotData(data, lockedJoints={'panda_finger_joint1':0.04, 'panda_finger_joint2':0.04})
  robot = RobotFromURDFdata(data, PDcontrol=(1e4, 1e2))
```



Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`reduceURDFrobotDataTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/reduceURDFrobotDataTest.py) (TM)


(sec-urdfimport-robotmodeldictfromdata)=
## Function: RobotModelDictFromData

[`RobotModelDictFromData(robotData)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L766)

- **function description**: The part of a model of robotics.models given by a URDF, as Python text, from the data of GetURDFrobotData (#3373): the links in the joint frames of the URDF, for dhMode 'jointFrames'; what a URDF does not give is added by hand to the dict.
- **input**:

- **output**: a string with the Python text of the list of the links, each with name, parent, jointType, jointLimits, preHT, mass, COM, inertia and, if the link has them, collisionShapes


(sec-urdfimport-fitcapsuletopoints)=
## Function: FitCapsuleToPoints

[`FitCapsuleToPoints(points)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L808)

- **function description**: A small capsule that contains all given points, the simple collision shape of a link (#3374).
- **input**:
  - `points`: the points, an array of shape (n, 3), for example of a collision mesh
- **output**: dict with type 'capsule' and pAxis, vAxis, radius as for graphics.Capsule: pAxis and pAxis+vAxis are the centers of its two spheres; the principal axis of the points giving the smallest volume is taken; vAxis is zero for a sphere


(sec-urdfimport-fitcapsulestomesh)=
## Function: FitCapsulesToMesh

[`FitCapsulesToMesh(points, triangles = None, numberOfCapsules = 2, minimumGain = 1.)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L873)

- **function description**: Small capsules that together contain a mesh, for the collision shapes of a link: for a link that is bent, several capsules are much closer to it than one (#3382). The points are divided by their distance to the axes of the capsules, which are fitted again; all points on the surface are in one of the capsules.
- **input**:
  - `points`: the points of the mesh, an array of shape (n, 3)
  - `triangles`: None or the triangles of the mesh, an array of point indices: points are added on long triangles, as the capsules must also contain these
  - `numberOfCapsules`: the number of capsules
  - `minimumGain`: the capsules are only returned if the volume of their union is below minimumGain times the volume of a single capsule; else one capsule is returned
- **output**: the list of dicts as returned by FitCapsuleToPoints


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotCollisionShapesTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCollisionShapesTest.py) (TM)


(sec-urdfimport-collisionshapesfromgeometry)=
## Function: CollisionShapesFromGeometry

[`CollisionShapesFromGeometry(geometry, meshesAs = 'capsules', numberOfCapsules = 2)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L912)

- **function description**: The collision shapes of a RobotLink from the collision geometries of GetURDFrobotData (#3382).
- **input**:
  - `geometry`: the list of the key 'collision' of a link, or 'collisionBase', of GetURDFrobotData
  - `meshesAs`: 'capsules': all meshes of the list together by FitCapsulesToMesh, for a fast check; 'convex': each mesh as the points of its convex hull, which requires scipy
  - `numberOfCapsules`: the number of capsules for the meshes of the list
- **output**: the list of shapes, the box, cylinder and sphere as they are


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotCollisionShapesTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCollisionShapesTest.py) (TM)


(sec-urdfimport-convexhullofmesh)=
## Function: ConvexHullOfMesh

[`ConvexHullOfMesh(points, triangles, name = '', verbose = 1)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L937)

- **function description**: The convex hull of a triangle mesh, as the contacts of polytopes need it, and how convex the mesh is (#3374).
- **input**:
  - `points`: the points of the mesh, an array of shape (n, 3)
  - `triangles`: the triangles of the closed mesh, an array of shape (m, 3) of point indices
  - `name`: the name written in the warning
  - `verbose`: if larger than 0, a warning is printed where the volume of the mesh is less than 0.98 of its hull
- **output**: [hullPoints, hullTriangles, ratio], the triangles oriented outward and ratio the volume of the mesh divided by that of the hull
- **notes**: requires scipy


(sec-urdfimport-robotfromurdfdata)=
## Function: RobotFromURDFdata

[`RobotFromURDFdata(robotData, gravity = [0, 0, -9.81], baseHT = None, toolHT = None, PDcontrol = (None, None), urdfFile = None, enableEndStops = False, collisionMeshesAs = 'capsules')`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L984)

- **function description**: Create a Robot from the data of GetURDFrobotData (or of a dict of it loaded from a file): the links with their parents, masses, inertias, joint limits and graphics, the base graphics and the tool frame (#3356). A Robot is saved with its graphics by Robot.SaveToHDF5, and loaded without the packages that read the URDF.
- **input**:
  - `robotData`: the dict of GetURDFrobotData
  - `gravity`: the gravity vector of the robot
  - `baseHT`: None or the homogeneous transformation of the base
  - `toolHT`: None or the frame of the tool relative to the last link; None: the 'toolHT' of robotData (argument toolLinkName of GetURDFrobotData), else the frame of the last link
  - `PDcontrol`: (P, D), the same for all joints, or a list of one (P, D) per joint; (None, None): no control
  - `urdfFile`: None or a URDF file (not xacro) from which the elements dynamics of the joints are read, as viscous friction (damping) and Coulomb friction (friction) of the links, since release 1.5 of the Robotics Toolbox does not read them; this may change with a later release
  - `enableEndStops`: enableEndStops of Robot; the limits of the joints are stored in the links in any case
  - `collisionMeshesAs`: how the collision meshes of robotData (argument collision of GetURDFrobotData) become collision shapes, see CollisionShapesFromGeometry
- **output**: the Robot; a joint without limits (upper not larger than lower) has jointLimits=None

*example*:

```python
  data = GetURDFrobotData(LoadURDFrobot('urdf/robot.urdf', packagePath)['robot'], toolLinkName='tool0')
  robot = RobotFromURDFdata(data, PDcontrol=(1e4, 1e2))
  robot.SaveToHDF5('robot.h5')
```



Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/serialRobotURDF.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/serialRobotURDF.py) (Ex), [`reduceURDFrobotDataTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/reduceURDFrobotDataTest.py) (TM), [`robotFromURDFdataTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotFromURDFdataTest.py) (TM)


(sec-urdfimport-makecorkerobot)=
## Function: MakeCorkeRobot

[`MakeCorkeRobot(robotDic)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L1047)

- **function description**: makeCorkeRobot, creates robot using the peter corke toolbox using standard (stdDH) or modified (modKKDH) Denavid Hartenberg parameters
- **input**:
  - `robotDic`: robot dictionary by exudyn robotic models, its 'dhMode' stdDH for standard DH parameters, modKKDH for modified ones
- **output**: serial robot object by corke
- **author**: Martin Sereinig
- **notes**: DH Parameter Information: stdH = [theta, d, a, alpha] with Rz(theta) * Tz(d) * Tx(a) * Rx(alpha) modDH = [alpha, dx, theta, rz] with used by Corke and Lynch: Rx(alpha) * Tx(a) * Rz(theta) * Tz(d) used by Khali:           Rx(alpha) * Tx(d) * Rz(theta) * Tz(r) Important note:  d(khali)=a(corke)  and r(khali)=d(corke)


(sec-urdfimport-loadurdfgraphics)=
## Function: LoadURDFgraphics

[`LoadURDFgraphics(urdfFile, packagePath = None, color = None, invertTriangles = False, orientTriangles = True, smoothNormals = True, smoothingAngle = 0.25*np.pi, addEdges = False)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L1104)

- **function description**: the visual meshes of the links of a URDF file as Exudyn graphics, without the Robotics Toolbox (#3263): for each <link> its <visual> elements with a mesh of an STL file (binary or text, read by graphics.FromSTLfile), their <origin> and scale, and the color of their <material>; meshes of other formats and the shapes box, cylinder, sphere are skipped with a warning. The triangles of STL files are often not oriented consistently, and their normals are those of the triangles: the options invert them, orient them (graphics.OrientTriangles) and smoothen the normals (graphics.AddEdgesAndSmoothenNormals), as the meshes of a URDF need
- **input**:
  - `urdfFile`: the path of the URDF file
  - `packagePath`: the directory that contains the packages of the mesh file names package://package/...; None: the directory above the package of the URDF file (the layout package/urdf/robot.urdf of ROS packages)
  - `color`: None, the colors of the URDF materials (grey without one); or one RGBA color for all meshes
  - `invertTriangles`: if True, the orientation of the triangles of the STL files inverted, for meshes that come inside out; STL files and Exudyn have the corners counterclockwise seen from outside (#3275)
  - `orientTriangles`: if True, then the triangles of each mesh oriented consistently, closed parts and open parts that enclose a volume (the meshes of many URDFs have gaps) outward (graphics.OrientTriangles); another open surface keeps the orientation that most of its triangles have
  - `smoothNormals`: if True, the normals smoothened at the points, except at edges sharper than smoothingAngle; else the normals of the triangles
  - `smoothingAngle`: the angle between two triangles (in radians) above which their common edge stays sharp
  - `addEdges`: if True, the sharp edges added as lines
- **output**: a dict of the link names to lists of graphics data in the frame of the link


(sec-urdfimport-addurdfgraphics)=
## Function: AddURDFgraphics

[`AddURDFgraphics(robot, urdfFile, linkNames, baseLinkName = None, packagePath = None, color = None, **options)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/urdfImport.py#L1178)

- **function description**: the graphics of a Robot from the visual meshes of a URDF file (#3263), for a robot whose link frames are the frames of the URDF links, as the models of exudyn.robotics.models with dhMode 'jointFrames' (e.g. ManipulatorStaubliTX2_90L, whose dict names the URDF and its links in 'urdfGraphics'); the joint and COM graphics of the links switched off; further keyword arguments go to LoadURDFgraphics (invertTriangles, orientTriangles, smoothNormals, smoothingAngle, addEdges)
- **input**:
  - `robot`: the exudyn.robotics.Robot
  - `urdfFile`: the path of the URDF file
  - `linkNames`: the names of the URDF links of the robot links, one per link
  - `baseLinkName`: None, or the name of the URDF link of the base
  - `packagePath`: as LoadURDFgraphics
  - `color`: as LoadURDFgraphics


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/serialRobotInteractiveLimits.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/serialRobotInteractiveLimits.py) (Ex), [`robotics/staubliTX2blending.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/staubliTX2blending.py) (Ex), [`robotics/staubliTX2trajectories.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/staubliTX2trajectories.py) (Ex)
